title: Ajai Alai
subtitle: Ik Achhree Chhand from Jaap Sahib — Unconquerable, Undying, Fearless, Ageless
theme: A prayer for courage, fearlessness and unshakeable strength
intention: Sing this when you need to stand firm — before a difficult conversation, an exam, a shift, a decision you cannot walk away from. Each word is a name of the One who cannot be defeated.

source.granth: Sri Dasam Granth Sahib — Jaap Sahib

keywords: Ajai Alai Abhai Abai Abhu Aju Anas Akas
Na Rage Na Range Na Roope Na Rekhe
Jaap Sahib Guru Gobind Singh Ji

verses.s: Invencible, inmortal, sin miedo, sin edad.

verses.e: Beyond the elements, unborn, imperishable, all-pervading like the sky.
verses.s: Más allá de los elementos, no nacido, imperecedero, omnipresente como el cielo.

verses.e: Indestructible, unbreakable, invisible, needing no sustenance.
verses.s: Indestructible, irrompible, invisible, sin necesidad de sustento.

verses.e: Timeless, merciful, beyond all reckoning, without any religious garb.
verses.s: Atemporal, compasivo, más allá de todo cálculo, sin vestimenta religiosa alguna.

verses.e: Nameless, desireless, unfathomable, impossible to tear down.
verses.s: Sin nombre, sin deseo, insondable, imposible de derribar.

verses.e: Without a master, the supreme destroyer of evil, not born from a womb, not bound by vows of silence.
verses.s: Sin amo, supremo destructor del mal, no nacido de vientre alguno, no atado a votos de silencio.

verses.g: ਨ ਰਾਗੇ ॥ ਨ ਰੰਗੇ ॥ ਨ ਰੂਪੇ ॥ ਨ ਰੇਖੇ ॥
verses.h: न रागे ॥ न रंगे ॥ न रूपे ॥ न रेखे ॥
verses.t: Na raage na range na roope na rekhe.
verses.e: Without attachment, without colour, without form, without outline.
verses.s: Sin apego, sin color, sin forma, sin contorno.

verses.e: Beyond karma, beyond illusion, indestructible, beyond all reckoning.
verses.s: Más allá del karma, más allá de la ilusión, indestructible, más allá de todo cálculo.

meaning: “Ajai Alai” (ਅਜੈ ਅਲੈ) opens the Ik Achhree Chhand of Jaap Sahib and means “Unconquerable, Undying.” Almost every word in the passage begins with the negating prefix a- (“without” or “beyond”): jai is conquest, so ajai is the One who cannot be conquered; bhai is fear, so abhai is the One who is without fear. Line by line, Guru Gobind Singh Ji describes the Creator by removing every human limit — birth, age, name, form, colour and karma.

Ik Achhree Chhand (also written Ik Achhri or Ek Akhri Chhand) is named for its meter: each unit is a single short word, set off by ॥, four to a line. It forms chhands 189–196 of Jaap Sahib, the opening composition of Sri Dasam Granth Sahib, which Sikhs recite daily as part of Nitnem and at Amrit Sanchar.

Sung at pace, the short words land like steady footsteps. That is why MedRise Gurbani offers it as a shabad for courage — before an exam, a hard conversation, a shift or a race — as a reminder that the One you lean on cannot be defeated.
faq: Ajai means unconquerable and alai means undying — the One who can never be defeated and never passes away. The line continues “abhai abai”: fearless and ageless.
Where is Ajai Alai found and who wrote it?
It is the Ik Achhree Chhand of Jaap Sahib (chhands 189–196), the first bani of Sri Dasam Granth Sahib, composed by Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
A meter in which each unit is one short word. It is spelled many ways — Ik Achhree, Ik Achhri, Ek Akhri Chhand — and all refer to this passage of Jaap Sahib.
Why do so many words start with “A”?
“A-” is a negating prefix meaning “without” or “beyond.” The passage describes God by what God is not: not conquered, not born, not named, not bound by form or karma.
Is Ajai Alai part of Nitnem?
Yes. Jaap Sahib is one of the daily Nitnem banis, and this passage is recited within it.
